state.case_summary:
A 29-year-old healthy man noted persistent swelling of his left breast for four years. Initially, ultrasonography had shown gynecomastia (BIRADS II) attributed to anabolic-steroid use, which he discontinued. He now reports a new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass under the left nipple. Repeat ultrasonography demonstrates a 1.5-cm long, solid structure with lobular architecture. Mammography reveals a lobulated retroareolar mass approximately 1.5 cm in diameter without microcalcifications (BIRADS III).

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A. Intraductal papilloma
B. a male breast lump comprising gynecomastia, fibroadenoma and lipoma
C. due to papillary architecture on imaging, but the lack of microcalcifications lowered malignancy risk

E. Fibroadenoma and lipoma were included among common benign male breast masses but are less consistent with a discrete

G. Intracystic papillary and invasive carcinomas were suspected due to papillary architecture on imaging, but the lack of
H. The absence of stromal invasion on tissue sections excludes invasive carcinoma
